walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1543 Vesalius published On the Fabric of the Human Body.

He dissected human corpses and corrected Galen's mistakes. In 1628 William Harvey proved the heart pumps blood around the body — a complete circuit.

In 1854 John Snow traced a London cholera outbreak to the Broad Street pump.

In 1861 Louis Pasteur published germ theory — microbes cause disease. From 1867 Joseph Lister used carbolic acid in surgery, slashing infection rates.

In 1928 Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from a mould.

Florey and Chain mass-produced it in WWII. In 1948 the NHS was launched, giving free healthcare to everyone in Britain at the point of use.

Harvey
Pasteur

mcqs.q: In what year was the NHS launched in Britain?
Why was Vesalius significant in the history of medicine?
options: The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.
His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.

mcqs.q: What was Pasteur's contribution to medicine?
options: The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Pasteur invented antibiotics like penicillin.
Pasteur invented the stethoscope.
He proved germ theory of disease via experiments on fermentation and spontaneous generation, then developed vaccines for rabies and anthrax — Koch identified specific bacteria.

mcqs.q: What was the theory of the four humours?
options: Disease was caused by imbalance of blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile; treatment aimed to rebalance them via bloodletting, purging or diet. It dominated for nearly 2,000 years.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Pasteur invented the stethoscope.
Medieval doctors knew about germs but used humours because they had no medicine.
